top_fixes: Make the corner tag concrete. 'AT THE END: THE JOB' means nothing to a cold viewer. Use something like 'AT THE END: THE AI JOB SALESFORCE IS HIRING FOR', and pulse that tag at beat 19→20 so the Salesforce turn reads as the promised payoff and not a second reel.

Fix the contradiction between beat 6 and beat 12. 'Only one got STOP' is followed by a second STOP on the lunge, so viewers think the count is wrong. Make the lunge visibly judge-only, for example 'The judge alone said STOP' with on-screen 'JUDGE ONLY · NOT FINAL', and reserve the full red STOP stamp for the reverse crunch.

Put steps 1 and 2 in body words for the mass group. 'Each dip in the wave' is where most non-builders leave. Tie the wave to the limb on screen, for example 'Two: knee bends, the line dips. One dip, one rep', and pulse the wave in sync with the visible rep.

Cut text density on the short beats. Beat 2 has three labels in 2.7 s and beat 20 has four disclaimer items in 3.1 s, which nobody can read. Use at most two elements per beat, and hold 'REPORTEDLY · NOT CONFIRMED' as one small persistent line across beats 20-22.

Move the gym-buddy send from 6.6 s to after the proof, at beats 17-18, as TRIAL already does. In its place at beat 3, state the cost in gym words using a number from FACTS. Soften 'never have done' or back it with that cost, because the trainer reads STOP as overclaiming for a short rep. Also change the loop: cutting from the job posting to the ghost frame is a non-sequitur, so end on a line or frame that points back to the hook.

top_fixes: Say in frame one what 'my AI' is. Add an on-screen line such as 'I BUILT AN AI THAT WATCHES MY GYM VIDEOS' under beat 1, because personas 2, 4, 5 and 16 never learn what they're watching. Consider leading with the TRIAL hook ('My AI told me to stop my set. It was wrong.'), which is the more sendable story for non-builders, but drop 'So I fixed it' from T3, since it resolves the loop at 6 s.

Speak the open loop before the five steps instead of leaving it to corner tags. Beat 7 is where six of the 16 leave. A line like 'It also got one wrong. First, how it knows.' gives non-builders a reason to sit through steps 1-4; the tags are too small to carry that promise.

Cut on-screen text to one idea per beat. Beat 2 (two angles plus SAME SET in 2.7 s), beat 10 (two clips and three text blocks in 2.3 s) and beat 20 (four-part disclaimer in 3.1 s) can't be read at that pace. Drop '30 FPS' and 'Fable 5.2', keep one clip in beat 10, and shrink the attribution to small persistent source text.

Make step 2 self-explanatory on screen. 'Each dip in the wave' assumes the viewer knows what the wave is. Show the knee angle drawing the line live with a rep counter ticking on each dip, and label it 'KNEE ANGLE', so the trainer and finance viewers follow without the audio.

Hold viewers through the pivot to the job. 'Comment FORM' at 48 s reads as the end, so gym viewers swipe before the tease, and the people who care about the Salesforce line (3, 8, 10) left 35 s earlier. Say the job promise aloud once at beat 6, keep COMMENT FORM on screen through beats 20-22, and end on one concrete detail from the posting, not just 'Next: how to get it'.

top_fixes: Make the middle readable for non-tech viewers without touching the five steps: cut each step's on-screen text to the counter plus one plain phrase (e.g. '3/5 · CAN'T SEE THE KNEE? NO VERDICT'), and drop '30 FPS', 'REP MATHS' and the stacked hand-off questions where the voice already carries them.
